questions.question:
You are asked to set up RBAC for a CI/CD pipeline.

Create a new ClusterRole named `deployment-clusterrole` which only allows the creation of the following resource types:

- `Deployment`
- `StatefulSet`
- `DaemonSet`

Create a new ServiceAccount named `cicd-token` in the existing namespace `app-team1`.

Bind the new ClusterRole `deployment-clusterrole` to the new ServiceAccount `cicd-token`, limited to the namespace `app-team1`.

Note: the binding must restrict the ServiceAccount to the `app-team1` namespace only - it must not be able to create Deployments in any other namespace.

verification.description: ClusterRole deployment-clusterrole exists with only 'create' on deployments/statefulsets/daemonsets
ServiceAccount cicd-token exists in app-team1
Binding is namespace-scoped to app-team1 (RoleBinding to the ClusterRole), not cluster-wide

questions.question:
A node in the cluster has been labeled `drain-target=true` and is currently running workloads from the `node-ops/drain-target` Deployment.

Mark the node labeled `drain-target=true` as unschedulable, and safely evict/reschedule all non-DaemonSet pods running on it, so that its workloads continue running elsewhere in the cluster.

Use the standard `kubectl cordon` and `kubectl drain` workflow (the node should remain cordoned afterwards).

verification.description: The node labeled drain-target=true is cordoned (spec.unschedulable=true)
All drain-target Deployment pods are rescheduled off the cordoned node and Running

questions.question:
First, create a snapshot of the running etcd cluster and save it to `/tmp/exam/etcd-snapshot.db`.

Then, verify the snapshot is valid by restoring it into a new local data directory `/tmp/exam/etcd-restored`.

This environment is not the real exam environment: use etcd endpoint `https://k8s-api-server:2379`, with client certificates located at:

- CA cert: `/home/candidate/.kube/etcd-certs/ca.crt`
- Client cert: `/home/candidate/.kube/etcd-certs/client.crt`
- Client key: `/home/candidate/.kube/etcd-certs/client.key`

Example commands:

`ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/exam/etcd-snapshot.db --endpoints=https://k8s-api-server:2379 --cacert=/home/candidate/.kube/etcd-certs/ca.crt --cert=/home/candidate/.kube/etcd-certs/client.crt --key=/home/candidate/.kube/etcd-certs/client.key`

`ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot restore /tmp/exam/etcd-snapshot.db --data-dir=/tmp/exam/etcd-restored`

verification.description: /tmp/exam/etcd-snapshot.db exists, is a non-trivial size, and passes 'etcdctl snapshot status'
/tmp/exam/etcd-restored is a structurally valid etcd data directory produced by 'etcdctl snapshot restore'

questions.question:
Create a NetworkPolicy named `allow-port-from-namespace` in namespace `fubar` which allows pods in namespace `internal` to connect to port `9000` of pods in namespace `fubar`.

More specifically, ensure that:

- The policy allows pods in the `internal` namespace to connect to port `9000/tcp` of ALL pods in namespace `fubar`.
- The policy does NOT allow access from any other namespace.
- The policy does NOT allow access to any other port.

Tip: every namespace already carries the built-in immutable label `kubernetes.io/metadata.name` equal to its own name, so you can select the `internal` namespace with a `namespaceSelector` without labeling it yourself.

verification.description: NetworkPolicy allow-port-from-namespace exists in fubar
Ingress rule restricts source to namespace 'internal' and port 9000/TCP only
podSelector is empty, applying the policy to all pods in fubar

verification.description: front-end Deployment's nginx container has a port named 'http' = 80/TCP

questions.question:
Pod `foo` is running and periodically writing log lines, some of which contain the literal string `error file-not-found`.

Extract only the log lines containing the literal string `error file-not-found` from pod `foo`'s logs and write them to `/tmp/exam/foo-errors.log` (the file already exists, currently empty).

Do not include any non-matching lines in the file.

verification.description: foo-errors.log contains only 'error file-not-found' lines and at least one is present

questions.question:
Pod `big-corp-app` has a single container which writes to the file `/var/log/big-corp-app.log`, via an `emptyDir` volume already mounted at `/var/log`.

Add a second, "sidecar" container named `sidecar` to the Pod `big-corp-app`, using image `busybox`, which continuously tails (`tail -f`) that same log file.

Note: containers cannot be added to a running Pod - you will need to delete and recreate the Pod `big-corp-app` with the additional container, keeping the existing container and volume configuration intact.

verification.description: Pod big-corp-app has exactly 2 containers
A container named 'sidecar' uses image busybox and mounts the same volume at /var/log
'kubectl logs big-corp-app -c sidecar' returns non-empty log output

questions.question:
Several Pods labeled `name=overloaded-cpu` are running in the `monitoring` namespace, each consuming a different amount of CPU.

Find the Pod (among those labeled `name=overloaded-cpu`) that is consuming the most CPU (via `kubectl top pod`), and write just its name to `/tmp/exam/top-cpu-pod.txt` (the file already exists, currently empty).

verification.description: top-cpu-pod.txt contains the name of the pod with the highest CPU usage

questions.question:
Create a new StorageClass named `csi-hostpath-sc` with `allowVolumeExpansion: true`.

Note: this environment uses the kind built-in `rancher.io/local-path` provisioner in place of the real exam's `csi-hostpath-driver`, since no CSI driver is pre-installed - use provisioner `rancher.io/local-path` and you must also set `volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer` on the StorageClass - `rancher.io/local-path` requires it to know which node to provision the volume on, and the PVC will stay stuck `Pending` without it.

Create a PersistentVolumeClaim named `pv-volume` using that StorageClass, requesting `10Mi` of storage with access mode `ReadWriteOnce`.

Create a Pod named `web-server` using image `nginx` which mounts that PersistentVolumeClaim at `/usr/share/nginx/html`.

Finally, expand the PersistentVolumeClaim `pv-volume` to `70Mi` (edit/patch its requested storage).

verification.description: StorageClass csi-hostpath-sc exists with allowVolumeExpansion=true
PVC pv-volume uses csi-hostpath-sc with access mode ReadWriteOnce
PVC pv-volume is Bound
Pod web-server mounts pv-volume at /usr/share/nginx/html and is Running
PVC pv-volume requested storage was patched to 70Mi

questions.question:
Create an Ingress resource named `pong` in namespace `ing-internal` as follows:

- Uses the `nginx` IngressClass
- Exposes the existing Service `hello` (ClusterIP, port `5678`) on path `/hello`
- Uses pathType `Prefix`

An ingress-nginx controller is already installed in the cluster, and the `hello` Service/Deployment already exist in `ing-internal`.

verification.description: Ingress pong exists in ing-internal
Ingress uses the nginx ingress class
Ingress has a Prefix rule for /hello routing to service hello:5678
